thread:
maria-support: FYI customer BrightWave reporting sudden p95 spikes and 504s on their dedicated eu1 pool since ~09:12 UTC. They see degraded throughput for inference jobs.
kevin-sre: thanks — any recent autoscale events or pool config changes?
maria-support: autoscaler logs show a single scale-up attempt at 09:15 but it failed with "scale-rejected: node-throttle". Customer says latency spike started before failed scale.
alex-infra: grabbing node list and MIG allocations now. Can you share tenant id and pool id?
maria-support: tenant brightwave-01, pool eu1-ded-42, node id gpu-node-07. Customer attached a snippet of `nvidia-smi` from their side showing MIG partitions changed mid-run.
nina-eng: ugh. sounds like noisy neighbor MIG reconfiguration. Do we have GPU health traces? PCIe/link errors?
maria-support: attaching paste of their logs (shortened):
```
09:11:43 INFO request id=... start seq
09:12:02 WARN p90 latency 340ms p95 1.2s
09:12:18 ERROR 504 upstream timeout
09:13:01 INFO node-metrics gpu-node-07: mem-util 84% sm 72% temperature 76C
09:13:05 NOTICE mig-reconfig: partitions 7->4
09:14:30 ERROR autoscale: rejected scale reason=node-throttle
```
kevin-sre: the `mig-reconfig` line is concerning. If another tenant resized MIG slices, that can evict resources and cause KV-cache misses, plus kernel context-switch cost.
alex-infra: I see node-events around 09:13 on our side too: "hostd: reconfigure_mig" from tenant ops stream on same host. We'll check scheduling logs to see if live-reconfig was allowed.
maria-support: customer claims no maintenance. They ran a large ephemeral training job at that time. Could be they used reserved MIG reassign via API.
nina-eng: quick repro steps we should request from customer: 1) exact command that started training 2) `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=uuid,mig.mode.current --format=csv` before/after 3) a warmup trace of kvcache hit rates. Also ask for per-request model/seq lengths.
sam-cs: customer worried about billing — they saw spikes in token usage and errors. Is there an automatic crediting flow for platform-caused degradations?
kevin-sre: raise an internal incident flag. If platform reconfiguration caused eviction, ops team needs to audit tenant operations for unauthorized MIG changes on dedicated hosts. Tagging @ops-bot to create an incident.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0896 — "Potential MIG reconfiguration causing tenant eviction in eu1-ded-42". Assigned to infra/host-ops. Priority P1?
alex-infra: initial findings: host-ops logs show a tenant-initiated `mig.reconfigure` call from tenant id training-hub-99 at 09:12:58. That call briefly reduced total available slices on gpu-node-07. Scheduling allowed it because quota checks passed; however, it collided with high inference load from BrightWave.
maria-support: customer will repro with a controlled run. They asked for mitigation steps in the meantime.
nina-eng: mitigation options: 1) temporarily pin BrightWave to nodes with fixed MIG profiles (no live-mig allowed), 2) increase autoscale aggressive threshold so scale-up happens earlier, or 3) enable isolation mode on pool (reject live-mig ops on shared hosts).
alex-infra: quick patch we can apply: set pool flag `disallow-live-mig=true` on eu1-ded-42 until we finish root-cause. That will force any tenant mig ops to be queued. Need approval from infra leads.
kevin-sre: do it and notify customers. Also collect kernel ring buffer from gpu-node-07: `sudo dmesg | tail -n 200` and `journalctl -u host-agent --since "2026-03-01 09:00" | grep mig`.
maria-support: forwarding mitigation options to BrightWave; they prefer pinning nodes for now. They've requested a postmortem and possible credit for the 30m outage window.
sam-cs: noted. I'll log a billing review and link to INC-2026-0896.
ops-bot: Action items created: 1) infra: apply disallow-live-mig on pool eu1-ded-42 (owner: alex-infra) 2) host-ops: collect dmesg/journals from gpu-node-07 and audit tenant mig API calls (owner: kevin-sre) 3) support: get repro artifacts from customer (owner: maria-support).
kevin-sre: long-term fix brainstorm: enforce host-level policy that live MIG reconfigs are disallowed on any host with active dedicated tenants above a threshold, or require cross-tenant reconfigations to go through maintenance window.
nina-eng: also consider adding an autoscaler signal for "mig-churn" that temporarily raises scale aggressiveness when we detect partition changes. Could prevent transient p95 spikes.
maria-support: customer confirmed repro run scheduled for 11:00 UTC; they've asked for a contact during repro. I'll update thread after we get artifacts. :white_check_mark:
kevin-sre: thanks — keep thread updated. If customer provides `nvidia-smi -q` snapshots we'll attach to the incident.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0896 updated: status=investigating, priority=P1, linked threads=1.
